autonomous-ai-agent.main: Home Autonomous AI agent Autonomous AI agent An autonomous AI agent is software that takes multi-step actions toward a goal without you typing every instruction at each step. On Krafty Bot, autonomy shows up as routines, unattended chat turns, and work on a shared cloud computer—with approvals before changes to your apps or risky clicks. Updated October 26, 2026 Start free How Krafty Bot works What people mean by autonomous Usually: the agent plans steps, uses tools, and keeps going for a while without live chat. It does not mean unlimited freedom. Krafty Bots still hit plan usage limits, step caps, and approval gates described in the product docs. AI agent builder vs. describing a job Many products ship a visual builder or SDK. Krafty Bot is closer to hiring a teammate: you create a Bot, answer setup questions, and describe work in plain language. There is no separate canvas to wire nodes, though you can save a successful job as a routine. AI agents for business Manus alternatives How autonomy works on Krafty Bot Routines post a prompt into a chat on a schedule you choose Bots use connected apps and the shared cloud computer during a turn Unattended turns are labeled in the transcript so you can see what started them Continuations resume a capped turn without gaining new permissions Approvals wake the Bot when you decide on a held action FAQs Is Krafty Bot fully autonomous? No. It is built to keep working in the background, but writes to connected apps and committing computer steps require your approval unless you have allowed a specific action for that Bot. What is an AI agent builder in this context? Often a tool to compose tools and prompts visually. Krafty Bot instead uses chat instructions, per-Bot memory, and routines created from jobs that already worked. Where should I start? Pick a concrete job—expenses, triage, or a morning brief—on the business page or use-case library, then promote it to a routine when the Bot succeeds. how-it-works.main: Home How it works How Krafty Bot works Krafty Bot is an AI workspace where you hand Bots actual tasks, not just questions. Each Bot has its own memory and working instructions, and all the Bots on your account share one persistent cloud computer with a desktop and browser. Bots use the apps you connect, research the web, run routines on a schedule, and keep working after you close your browser. Updated October 26, 2026 Start free See use cases From a message to finished work Describe the job Create a Bot and tell it what you need. It asks a few setup questions, then saves its name, role, and working instructions. Connect the apps it needs The first time a task needs an app, the Bot asks you to connect it. You sign in yourself, and you can disconnect an app at any time. Let it work The Bot works in your apps and on its cloud computer, alone or with other Bots in a group chat. Ask it to repeat the job and it saves a routine that runs on a schedule. Review and approve When the Bot finishes, has a question, or wants to change something in a connected app, it tells you in the chat and on your Activity page. Changes wait for your approval. What every Bot has Its own memory Bots save notes to memory and recall them in any chat. Memory is separate from chat history, so tell a Bot what is worth remembering. A shared cloud computer Each account has one persistent cloud computer with a desktop and browser, shared by all its Bots. Files and browser sign-ins carry over from one Bot to the next. The computer pauses when idle and resumes when a Bot needs it. Your connected apps Bots find apps in a searchable catalog, such as Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, and Notion, and use them through the account you connect. Sites without a connection can be used in the computer's browser. Web research Bots search the web and read pages to answer questions and gather sources, with the searches counted against your plan's allowance. Routines on a schedule Bots run work daily, every few hours, or once at a set time, in your timezone. The free plan includes 1 routine and Pro up to 50. Group chats and handoffs Put several Bots in one chat and they pass work between themselves. A Bot can also brief a teammate and pick up the result. What waits for your approval Reading your connected apps needs no approval. Anything that writes to them, such as sending, posting, or updating a record, is held until you approve it, unless you have chosen to always allow that action for that Bot. High-risk app actions can never be set to always allow. On the cloud computer, a separate model checks each click and keypress against a screenshot, and steps that commit something run only after you approve them. Approval requests expire after seven days. Nothing in a web page, email, or document can approve an action; only you can. How it compares Compared with a chat assistant A chat assistant answers in a chat window while you watch. A Bot works in your apps and on its own computer, keeps going after you close the browser, and brings back finished work. Compared with workflow automation Automation tools run the exact steps you wire up ahead of time. You describe the job to a Bot in plain language, and it works out the steps, uses a browser when there's no integration, and asks you when something is unclear. What it doesn't do Bots don't remember everything automatically. They keep the notes you ask them to save. A task can stop early when you reach your usage allowance or step limit, or when a provider is down. The approval check on the computer is a model reading the screen. It reduces risk; it can't remove it. The free plan is for trying Krafty: one bot, one connected app, a one-time $1 AI allowance, and 5 minutes of computer time, once. What it costs Free: one bot, one connected app, a one-time $1 AI allowance, and 5 minutes of computer time, once. Pro: $20 per month for up to 50 bots, unlimited connected apps, a $10 AI allowance, and 50 hours of cloud computer time each billing period. People who sign in with their ChatGPT plan can run their Bots' model calls on that plan instead of the AI allowance. privacy.main: Privacy policy Last updated: October 26, 2026 Krafty provides AI teammates, connected tools, and cloud computers. This policy describes how information is handled when you use kraftybot.app and the Krafty mobile app. Krafty is operated by Drew Sepeczi. For privacy questions or requests, contact drewsepeczi@gmail.com . Information we collect Account information, including your email address, account identifier, and profile information provided when you sign up. Google sign-in provides basic identity information such as your name, email address, and profile picture. Sign in with Apple may provide your name and email address, including an Apple relay address if you hide your email. Content you provide or create, including messages, bot names and instructions, saved memories, files, and results generated while using your teammates. Voice recordings when you use dictation. Recording begins when you tap the wave button; stopping sends the audio for transcription. Cancelling before upload discards the recording. Only the transcript you choose to send becomes part of your conversation. If you report an AI response, we store the reported response text, your selected reason, any details you choose to add, the relevant account and conversation identifiers, and report and review dates to investigate the report. The report does not copy your full conversation or tool results. Connected-service information and permissions you authorize, including connection identifiers and the data your teammates retrieve or act on when you request work. Subscription and usage information, including your plan, subscription status, model usage, and cloud computer usage. Payment details are handled by our payment providers; Krafty does not receive your full payment card number. Technical and diagnostic information, including request details, device or browser information, account and task identifiers, and errors needed to operate and troubleshoot the service. How we use information We use information to authenticate you, provide your workspace, generate AI responses, perform the tasks you request, operate connected tools and cloud computers, retain conversation context and saved memories, meter usage, process subscriptions, provide support, and investigate errors or misuse. Google sign-in is used for authentication. Access to other services is a separate connection that you authorize. Connecting a service may allow a teammate to retrieve information or make changes within the permissions you grant. Service providers and AI processing Operating Krafty requires sharing relevant information with service providers. These include Clerk for authentication and subscription management, Stripe for payments, Railway for app hosting, Neon for database and AI gateway services, Anthropic for AI models, Trigger.dev for background tasks and conversations, E2B for cloud computers, Composio for connected tools, and Sentry for diagnostics. Messages, instructions, relevant conversation context, tool results, and files or screenshots needed for your request may be processed by AI model providers, directly or through our AI gateway. Providers process this information under their own applicable terms and privacy policies. Avoid submitting information you are not authorized to share. The mobile app asks for permission before enabling AI features. You can withdraw that permission under Account, then AI data sharing. Withdrawing permission prevents new AI activity from that app installation. It does not cancel work already running, change permissions on other devices, or delete information already processed. When your account uses your connected ChatGPT plan, OpenAI processes the conversation through that connection. Dictation sends your voice recording through Krafty to OpenRouter and Mistral for speech-to-text processing. Krafty does not save the audio in its database, and the mobile app removes its temporary recording after transcription, failure, or cancellation. Cancelling an upload cannot recall audio that a provider has already received. Providers process recordings under their own terms and privacy policies. We do not sell your personal information. We may disclose information when required by law, to protect users or the service, or as part of a transfer of the business, subject to applicable requirements. Cookies and storage We and our authentication provider use cookies and browser storage for sign-in, session security, and preferences. Blocking essential cookies may prevent sign-in or other features from working. The mobile app uses secure device storage for sign-in tokens and your AI-processing permission. App updates may use an installation identifier to deliver compatible software updates. The app does not display advertisements or use this information for cross-app advertising tracking. Retention and deletion Workspace content, saved memories, and cloud computer files may persist between sessions to support ongoing work. Logging out or disconnecting an integration does not by itself delete existing conversations, files, or memories. You can use available bot and conversation deletion controls. On iPhone, Account includes a Delete account control. You can also request deletion through the account deletion page or by contacting us. When account deletion completes, we delete your teammates, conversations and their history, memories, settings, cloud computer, and app and ChatGPT connections, cancel any paid subscription, and delete your sign-in account. Reports of AI responses are removed with the reported conversation or your account. We keep usage and billing records, which contain amounts and identifiers but no message content, for accounting. Trigger.dev, which runs your teammates’ conversations, processes your messages and replies. Copies of messages it handled can remain with Trigger.dev after you delete your account or a conversation. Task logs are retained according to our provider plan. We have not yet confirmed the retention period for message streams, task records, and previously saved conversation snapshots, or a supported way to erase those copies. Closing a conversation session does not delete them. We retain information as needed to provide the service and meet accounting, security, dispute-resolution, and legal requirements. Deletion may take time to complete across providers and backups. Data already sent to a connected service is also subject to that service’s controls and retention policies. Your choices and rights You can update available account settings, disconnect integrations, and revoke access in the connected provider’s settings. Depending on your location, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or obtain a copy of your information, or to object to certain processing. Send requests to drewsepeczi@gmail.com ; we may need to verify your identity. Security, international processing, and children We use account authentication and access controls to protect information. No online service can guarantee absolute security. Our providers may process information in countries outside your country of residence. Krafty is not intended for children under 13; contact us if you believe a child has provided personal information. Changes to this policy We may update this policy as the service changes and will update the date above. Where required, we will provide additional notice of material changes. Use of Krafty is also governed by our terms of service .

use-cases.main: Home Use cases AI teammate use cases Krafty Bot teammates sign in to your tools, work on their own cloud computer, and come back with finished work for you to review. Here are nine jobs to start with, each with a prompt you can paste into a new Bot and a page on what it does and what waits for your approval. Create your team View plans Sales Outbound Generate pipeline overnight. Researches accounts, scores contacts by intent, drafts email and LinkedIn in your voice, and leaves a review list for you to approve each morning. Try this prompt Copy Every weeknight at 2am, pull the HubSpot companies tagged “Target” that nobody has emailed in 30 days. For each, check their careers page and recent news for buying signals, find the VP of Engineering, and draft a three-sentence email in my voice based on my sent Gmail. Rank the top 10 in a Google Sheet with the signal behind each, and message me on Slack when it’s ready. Don’t send anything. How the Sales Outbound Bot works → Talent Scout Keep your talent pipeline moving. Sources candidates, drafts outreach in your voice, skips anyone already in the ATS, and handles interview scheduling once you approve. Try this prompt Copy Find 15 senior infrastructure engineers in the Bay Area who have worked at Series B to D startups, skipping anyone already in Greenhouse. Write each a short note that references their actual work, list them in a Google Sheet with links and why they fit, and once I approve, send the notes from my Gmail and offer three open slots from my Google Calendar. How the Talent Scout Bot works → Paid Media Protect your ad budget. Pulls live channel and campaign data every day, recommends reallocations against your monthly plan, and holds every bid change until you approve it. Try this prompt Copy Every morning at 8, pull yesterday’s spend, CTR, and conversions from Google Ads and Meta Ads and compare them to the monthly budget in my “Ad Plan” Google Sheet. Post a five-line summary in #growth on Slack. If a campaign has been above target CPA for three days running, recommend a specific reallocation and wait for my OK before changing anything. How the Paid Media Bot works → Expense Manager Close the week with clean books. Builds the weekly summary from your expense tool and sheets, files receipts from email, and nudges owners on missing categories before review. Try this prompt Copy Every Friday at 4pm, search my Gmail for this week’s receipts and invoices, save the PDFs to a “Receipts 2026” folder in Google Drive, and log the vendor, amount, date, and category of each in my “Expenses” Google Sheet. Flag anything over $500 or without a clear category, and DM the person who spent it on Slack to fill it in. How the Expense Manager Bot works → Product Performance Know what slowed down and why. Logs into observability tools, reads the flamegraphs, and comes back with the hot spots and a short writeup with screenshots. Try this prompt Copy Log into our Datadog, pull checkout p95 latency for the last 7 days, and compare it to the week before. If it’s up more than 20%, open the slowest traces, screenshot the flamegraphs, match the jump to a merged GitHub PR, and write a one-page Notion doc with the likely cause. Post the link in #eng-perf on Slack. How the Product Performance Bot works → Bug Reproduction Hand engineers bugs they can reproduce. Picks up the support thread, clicks the same path in staging, captures the failure, and drops a repro pack with steps and screenshots. Try this prompt Copy When a new Intercom conversation is tagged “bug”, follow the customer’s steps on our staging site in your browser. If it reproduces, capture screenshots and console errors, then open a Linear issue for the Web team with numbered repro steps, expected vs. actual behavior, and the customer’s plan. Reply in the Intercom thread’s internal notes with the link either way. How the Bug Reproduction Bot works → Account Health See risk and expansion before the QBR. Reads usage, CRM, and support signals across your book and ranks the accounts that need attention, with next steps. Try this prompt Copy Every Monday, pull every Salesforce account renewing in the next 90 days. For each, check seat usage in Stripe, open tickets in Zendesk, and the last email thread in my Gmail. Rank them by churn risk in a Google Sheet with one line of reasoning each, and draft a check-in email in Gmail for the five most at risk. How the Account Health Bot works → Chief of Staff Keep your week from slipping. Scans Slack, email, calendar, and meeting notes, flags what matches your priorities, and follows up on dropped threads before they go cold. Try this prompt Copy Every weekday at 7:30am, read my unread Gmail, Slack DMs, and today’s Google Calendar. Send me one Slack message with the meetings that need prep and a three-bullet brief on each attendee from our past emails, the emails that need a reply today with drafts waiting in Gmail, and any thread I promised to follow up on but haven’t. How the Chief of Staff Bot works → Support Triage Clear the queue before you log on. Triages new tickets, drafts replies grounded in your docs, files real bugs with repro steps, and escalates anything urgent to you. Try this prompt Copy Every hour, read new Zendesk tickets. Draft replies to how-to questions using our Notion help center, tag billing issues for finance, and for anything that looks like a bug, search Linear for an existing issue and link it or file a new one with repro steps. Post anything urgent in #support on Slack and tag me. How the Support Triage Bot works →
